problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the Build matrices step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses.
lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment; its first proof is the build step conclusion on the next push run, not the write receipt.
resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

problem: Commit regenerated matrices exited 1 at 42553597443, initially attributed to an unguarded commit on a clean tree.
failed_approach: Diagnosing from the step name instead of reading the step body; the workflow already wrapped commit/push in an if git diff --cached --quiet guard.
lesson: Read the workflow step body before proposing a repair; with the guard present, a step-7 exit 1 means the else-branch ran and commit or push itself failed.
correction: Misdiagnosis corrected; no workflow change required at that time.

problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list; never quote a log line that was not actually returned.

problem: The workflow's own commit step pushed a commit, so the branch head no longer matched the sha the proven check-run covered (pushed 187168f5, then 60b4d6cc, while the green check-run head stayed e3eba97e).
failed_approach: Treating a green run on the branch as sufficient for the merge gate.
lesson: Before merge_pr, take branch_head and the branch run list in the same turn and match run.sha to the exact head. A green run whose sha is an ancestor does not authorize the merge.

problem: Head 60b4d6cc, created by the workflow's own commit step, has no workflow run, so the exact-head check can never be met by polling.
failed_approach: Polling branch_head plus runs repeatedly for a run whose sha equals the self-commit head.
lesson: A push by a workflow step with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger a run. Push one allowed-path change yourself; once generated outputs are already committed the guarded commit makes no diff and the head stays put.

problem: PROGRESS.json under docs/venice-audit-v1/ is rewritten by the build step, so authored text there does not survive and editing it re-fires the guarded commit.
failed_approach: Forcing a fresh push run by editing docs/venice-audit-v1/PROGRESS.json.
lesson: Distinguish authored files from build outputs before choosing a push target. Force runs from tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py or the workflow file.

problem: Every push run regenerated docs/venice-audit-v1 outputs into a state differing from the committed files, so the guarded commit pushed a new head after each green run; the green run's sha was never the branch head and the exact-head merge gate could never pass by polling.
failed_approach: Repeatedly forcing fresh runs from allowed paths while leaving the job's git push in place.
lesson: When a workflow job pushes its own build output, no push-triggered run can certify the head it creates. Remove the push from the job (report drift instead) or make the build byte-stable; verify the head stops moving before attempting merge_pr.
resolution: Self-push removed at b05c9fc3; test forbids git push at 92de9357; both runs green and PR head_sha equals the newest run sha.
